# Applied Performance Digest: outline

Drafted 2026-10-04. The Digest is the successor to the Baylor Applied Performance Playbook
(internally titled the Operations Guide). Three parts: the handbook (who we are and how we
work), the ops manual (how we run each technology), and the NCAA tech items (how we adopt,
consent, store and hand over technology under the NCAA SSI recommendations).

## How to read this outline

- **Numbering.** Chapters are numbered in ship order, not reading order. Chapter 1 is the
  ForceDecks CMJ procedure (due 10/23) because it is the first thing a named user is waiting
  for. Parts are groupings; a reader opens the part they need.
- **Priority.** 1 = ships in the next three ship slots (by 12/4). 2 = this semester.
  3 = spring 2027 or when a user asks. Priorities follow the D1 rule: one piece every two
  weeks to a named user, logged in the status report, checked at 30 days.
- **Audience codes.** S = Applied Performance staff. I = interns and graduate assistants.
  C = coaches (sport and Athletic Performance). A = administrators and Athletic Medicine.
- **Source codes.** BG = Baylor Operations Guide (Nov 2025 docx). V3 = Revised Force Plate
  Testing V3. SOP = Technology SOP template. FP = Feb 2026 development plan. CL = Clemson
  playbook (structure only). IA = Iowa assessment manual (structure and ideas only).
  NCAA = Performance Technology Best Practices guide Draft v1 and forms A to E.
  MEM = facts from memory and notes listed in `sources.md`.
- **Format for every ops-manual chapter.** Iowa's front half (what the test is for,
  how often, how to read it) then the SOP template's back half (setup, athlete prep,
  protocol, data quality checks, troubleshooting, data management and export, contacts,
  revision history). Marked DRAFT until the named user has run it once.

## Part 1: Handbook

Who Applied Performance is, how it works, and what it expects. Mostly existing Baylor text,
tightened, with two new chapters borrowed in shape from Iowa.

| Ch | Title | Purpose | Audience | Source | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | How to use the Digest | One page: what the three parts are, who should read which, where the forms live, how to suggest a change. Replaces the missing table of contents. | S, I, C, A | FP sec 6, CL intro | 2 |
| H2 | Preparing Champions for Life; One Standard, One Accord | The Baylor mission, four pillars, six operating principles and 18 core values. Existing text, lightly edited. | S, I, C | BG | 3 |
| H3 | Health and Wellness: where Applied Performance sits | Missions of Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Mental Health Services, and how Applied Performance serves each. Existing text plus one paragraph on daily interaction. | S, I, C, A | BG, FP 3.1 | 3 |
| H4 | Applied Performance mission and operating principles | The four principles rewritten as short narratives with one Baylor example each (monitoring, evaluation and return-to-performance, collaboration, research). | S, I, C | BG, CL principles (shape), FP Phase 1 | 2 |
| H5 | Professional expectations | Social media, student-athlete interactions, confidentiality, data handling (points to Part 3), conduct. Written as expectations with examples, not rules with penalties, per leadership's stated preference. | S, I | CL policies (topics only), FP Phase 1, MEM 2026-07-30 | 2 |
| H6 | Why we test | Specific vs general tests, validity and reliability in plain words, familiarization trials, smallest meaningful change, when to reassess and when not to, how Baylor reads daily CMJ (baseline, Wednesday read, individualized thresholds). | S, I, C | IA (shape), MEM Flint baseline | 1 |
| H7 | Preparing the athlete for a test | The standard rules every ops-manual chapter points to: food and caffeine window, fatigue window, same time of day, fixed test order, the two testing conditions (in session, out of session) and their warm-ups. | S, I, C | IA (shape), V3 | 1 |
| H8 | Interns and graduate assistants | What to expect, daily responsibilities, the semester shape, and a pointer to the Intern_Curriculum project (Module 1 due 10/9). Does not absorb the curriculum. | I, S | CL intro and schedule (shape), FP sec 5 | 3 |

## Part 2: Ops manual

One chapter per technology or procedure, written from Baylor practice with device names,
storage locations and troubleshooting. Credentials are never printed; each chapter points to
the vault.

| Ch | Title | Purpose | Audience | Source | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **ForceDecks: countermovement jump procedure** | The full procedure for the test Baylor runs most: setup, athlete prep, protocol, data quality checks, troubleshooting, export, contacts. Draft in `ch01_forcedecks_cmj.md`. **Due 10/23.** | S, I | V3, BG ForceDecks section, SOP, IA (shape), MEM | 1 |
| O2 | Daily operations checklist | Morning and evening device list by name: charged, synced, stored. Who signs it. Weekly maintenance line. | I, S | CL checklist (shape), SOP, FP Phase 1 | 1 |
| O3 | Technology overview and sport assignments | One paragraph per device: what it measures, which sports use it, where it lives, who owns it. Expands the Operations Guide table. | S, I, C | BG table, FP Phase 2 | 2 |
| O4 | Credential and account management | Institutional admin accounts, the vault, who has access to what, what happens when someone leaves. Points to NCAA guide section 6 and Form C. | S | FP Phase 1, NCAA sec 6 | 2 |
| O5 | ForceDecks: other tests | Squat jump, hop test, single-leg CMJ, hands-free squat, isometric mid-thigh pull, isometric seated calf raise. Same format as chapter 1, shorter. | S, I | V3, BG, MEM (DSI) | 2 |
| O6 | Catapult GPS | The existing Catapult workflow (the one written from practice) with troubleshooting and the football vs Olympic sports account split made explicit. | S, I | BG Catapult section, CL Catapult (shape) | 2 |
| O7 | Data management and reporting pipeline | Where data goes after collection: vendor cloud (VALD Hub, OpenField, Perch, Polar) to Kitman Labs and the local database, to reports. File naming, retention, who may see what (points to NCAA guide section 4). | S, I | FP Phase 2, MEM (DuckDB, cmj-traffic-light), NCAA sec 4 | 2 |
| O8 | ForceFrame and NordBord | ForceFrame isometric tests; NordBord for return-to-play groups only, with the decision rule for when a demanding test is kept or dropped. | S, I | BG, MEM (NordBord retirement), CL ForceFrame (shape) | 3 |
| O9 | DynaMo | Handheld dynamometry and range of motion. | S, I | BG | 3 |
| O10 | Perch | Velocity-based training setup, rack mounting, exercise selection, what the metrics mean. Keeps the Operations Guide's Perch glossary. | S, I, C | BG | 3 |
| O11 | SmartSpeed and sprint testing | Timing gate setup plus how to read splits (acceleration, speed, combined, momentum). | S, I, C | BG, IA sprint entry (shape) | 3 |
| O12 | Polar heart rate | Strap fitting, pairing, session monitoring, what the metrics mean. | S, I | BG | 3 |
| O13 | Sport-specific data dictionaries | Per sport: the technologies used, the 5 to 8 metrics that matter, thresholds, reporting cadence. Pilot with 2 or 3 sports. | S, C | CL dictionary (shape), FP Phase 2 | 3 |
| O14 | Reporting templates and dashboards | Examples of the weekly and monthly reports coaches receive, with the metric selection rule (output, driver, strategy, symmetry). | S, C | FP Phase 2, MEM (metric framework) | 3 |
| O15 | Equipment inventory and maintenance | Serial numbers, purchase dates, warranty, storage, maintenance schedule. Lives as a table that O2 reads from. | S | FP Phase 2 | 3 |
| App | Appendices | Quick-reference cards (one per test), vendor support contacts, revision history for the whole Digest. | S, I | SOP | 2 |

## Part 3: NCAA tech items

The Performance Technology Best Practices guide (Draft v1, 2026-10-04) and its five forms
are the content. The Digest does not rewrite them. Each chapter here is a one-page staff
summary that links to the guide section and the form, written after Chris Ruf's three
decisions (due 10/14). Until then, Part 3 is a link to the guide.

| Ch | Title | Purpose | Audience | Source | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | What the NCAA asks and how Baylor answers | The SSI recommendations in a paragraph, the guide's purpose and scope, the working group and who owns the document. | S, C, A | NCAA sec 0 and 1 | 2 (after 10/14) |
| N2 | Adopting a new technology | How to request one, the intake form, how it is scored. | S, C | NCAA sec 2, Form E | 2 |
| N3 | Athlete consent and education | Notice vs consent, the consent form, annual re-consent, where records live, the education sessions. | S, C, A | NCAA sec 3, Form A | 2 |
| N4 | Data management rules for staff | Ownership, storage tiers, who may interpret and communicate data, collect only what is used, the transfer-athlete protocol. The rules chapter 1's data management section points to. | S, I | NCAA sec 4 | 2 |
| N5 | Vendor data contracts | The standard clause checklist and the exit clause; audit priority order. | S, A | NCAA sec 5, Form B | 3 |
| N6 | Staff transitions | Institutional admin accounts, access removal, the handover note, the offboarding checklist. | S, A | NCAA sec 6, Form C | 2 |
| N7 | Annual review and feedback | The athlete and staff surveys, the working group review, how the Digest itself gets revised. | S, A | NCAA sec 7, Form D | 3 |

## Ship order (first five slots)

| Slot | Date | Chapter | Named user to confirm |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10/23 | Ch 1 ForceDecks CMJ procedure | [CONFIRM: the staff member or intern who runs CMJ testing most days] |
| 2 | 11/6 | H7 Preparing the athlete, with H6 Why we test as its front matter | [CONFIRM: an Athletic Performance coach who schedules testing] |
| 3 | 11/20 | O2 Daily operations checklist | [CONFIRM: the intern or GA on morning setup] |
| 4 | 12/4 | N1 to N4 summaries, if Chris's decisions land by 10/14 | Chris Ruf |
| 5 | 12/18 | O7 Data management pipeline | [CONFIRM] |

## What is deliberately not in the Digest

- The intern curriculum (separate project, own cycle).
- Any device Baylor does not own (1080 Sprint, Proteus, Moxy, MuscleLab, PlyoMat, GymAware,
  Hawkin Dynamics).
- Credentials of any kind.
- Athlete-identifiable data, including in examples. Examples use made-up values.

Drafted 2026-10-04. The Digest is the successor to the Baylor Applied Performance Playbook
(internally titled the Operations Guide). Three parts: the handbook (who we are and how we
work), the ops manual (how we run each technology), and the NCAA tech items (how we adopt,
consent, store and hand over technology under the NCAA SSI recommendations).

## How to read this outline

- **Numbering.** Chapters are numbered in ship order, not reading order. Chapter 1 is the
  ForceDecks CMJ procedure (due 10/23) because it is the first thing a named user is waiting
  for. Parts are groupings; a reader opens the part they need.
- **Priority.** 1 = ships in the next three ship slots (by 12/4). 2 = this semester.
  3 = spring 2027 or when a user asks. Priorities follow the D1 rule: one piece every two
  weeks to a named user, logged in the status report, checked at 30 days.
- **Audience codes.** S = Applied Performance staff. I = interns and graduate assistants.
  C = coaches (sport and Athletic Performance). A = administrators and Athletic Medicine.
- **Source codes.** BG = Baylor Operations Guide (Nov 2025 docx). V3 = Revised Force Plate
  Testing V3. SOP = Technology SOP template. FP = Feb 2026 development plan. CL = Clemson
  playbook (structure only). IA = Iowa assessment manual (structure and ideas only).
  NCAA = Performance Technology Best Practices guide Draft v1 and forms A to E.
  MEM = facts from memory and notes listed in `sources.md`.

# Chapter 1: ForceDecks countermovement jump procedure

**DRAFT 0.1, 2026-10-04. Not yet run by a named user. Items marked [CONFIRM: ...] are
Baylor facts the author could not verify. Do not ship until they are resolved.**

Part 2, Ops manual. Applied Performance Digest.

| Owner | Daily user | Last reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| Director of Applied Performance | [CONFIRM: name and role of the staff member or intern who runs CMJ testing most days] | 2026-10-04 (draft) |

## The short version

Three countermovement jumps on the ForceDecks, hands on hips, after a weigh-in that reads
green. The athlete stands still, bends, jumps as high as they can, lands softly, and resets.
You review the three reps before you save. The whole thing takes about 90 seconds per athlete
once the plates are up.

## What this test is for

The countermovement jump (CMJ) is the test Applied Performance runs most, and it does three
jobs:

1. **Daily readiness.** Jumps during the week build each athlete's baseline. Modified
   reactive strength index (RSI-modified) is read against that baseline on Wednesdays, using
   percent change, a rolling average, and the smallest worthwhile change to tell a real drop
   from noise. Thresholds are individual, not one number for the team.
2. **Asymmetry.** Left and right plate forces show whether an athlete is loading one side
   more than the other. Useful monthly, and more often for an athlete returning from injury
   with Athletic Medicine.
3. **Training emphasis.** CMJ peak force divided by isometric mid-thigh pull peak force
   gives the dynamic strength index, which helps decide between more plyometric work and
   more maximal strength work. That needs the mid-thigh pull too; see chapter O5.

Because the same test serves three purposes, the procedure has to be the same every time.
A test can keep its name while the cue, the rep count or a software setting changes
underneath it, and the data will not tell you. That is why this chapter fixes all three in
writing.

**How often.** Daily or near-daily during training blocks for the readiness baseline
[CONFIRM: which sports jump daily, and which jump weekly]. Monthly asymmetry review.
Before and after a training phase for the dynamic strength index.

**What we report.** Pick a few metrics and keep them. The working rule is one or two output
metrics (jump height), one to three driver metrics (concentric impulse, eccentric braking
force), one to three strategy metrics (contraction time, countermovement depth), and
left-right asymmetry where it matters. Add anything else only with a reason written down.
[CONFIRM: the current reported metric set for daily readiness and for coach reports.]

## Setup

### Equipment

1. ForceDecks dual force plates [CONFIRM: model, serial numbers]
2. Laptop or tablet with the ForceDecks app [CONFIRM: device name and which app version, see note below]
3. Plate cables and power supply
4. Carrying case [CONFIRM: storage location, room and shelf]

Photo to add: full kit laid out and labeled.

### Location

A flat, hard, level floor with room for the athlete to jump and land without stepping off.
Rubber flooring is fine if the plates sit flat and do not rock. Near an outlet if the session
will run long.

Recommended locations: [CONFIRM: for example the main weight room, the Athletic Medicine
space, or a sport-specific facility].

### Software settings

Log in to the ForceDecks app with the department account. Credentials are in the vault, not
in this document. [CONFIRM: vault name and who has access.]

Confirm these settings before the first athlete steps on. They are the ones the current
Operations Guide lists:

- Layout, Operational Mode: Shared
- Layout, Show Profile Selection Pane: Always
- Platforms, Sequenced Platform Count: 1
- Platforms, Platform Assignment: matches the physical left and right plates
- Platforms, Auto Test Export Folder: the same folder as ForceDecks [CONFIRM: exact folder
  path, and whether the auto export is still used now that data goes to VALD Hub]

Note on app versions. The Operations Guide describes buttons called Weigh Start and Play.
Baylor's Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol describes Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and
Analyze and Save. These are two different versions of the ForceDecks software. This chapter
uses the V3 names. [CONFIRM: which version is installed on the testing device, and update
the button names to match.]

### Build the queue

Double-click profile names to add the athletes you are testing to the queue. Up to 16
profiles can be tested in one recording. If an athlete is new, create the profile first
[CONFIRM: naming convention for profiles, and whether the roster syncs from Kitman Labs or
is entered by hand].

### Zero the plates

Click Play (or Start). Make sure nothing is touching the plates, then let them zero. If a
cable, a shoe or a hand is on a plate during zeroing, every number that follows is wrong.

## Preparing the athlete

### Two testing conditions

**Condition 1: inside a training session.** The team warm-up is the warm-up. Test at the
same point in the session every time [CONFIRM: for example right after the warm-up and
before the first lift].

**Condition 2: outside a training session.** Run the standard warm-up from the V3 protocol:

- Line hops, forward and backward then left and right, 10 each
- Open gate and close gate (hip internal and external rotation), 5 each
- Rapid squat to stand (triple extension), 5

### Rules that keep the numbers comparable

These are the rules the handbook chapter "Preparing the athlete for a test" will carry. Until
it ships, they live here. They matter most for Condition 2 and for any test used before and
after a training phase. For daily readiness jumps inside a session, apply what you can and
note anything unusual.

- Same time of day as the athlete's previous tests, within reason.
- No food or caffeine in the two hours before a planned test.
- No hard session in the 48 hours before a planned test. If an athlete arrives obviously
  fatigued or sore, record the jump as a readiness data point but do not treat it as a
  baseline or a phase test. If it is a phase test, postpone it.
- Shoes: the same type the athlete trained in last time. Note a change.
- New athletes get at least three familiarization trials before their first recorded
  session. Someone who is still being coached through the movement will improve next time
  just from learning it, and that looks like a training effect.

### Explain the test

Tell the athlete: "Hands on your hips the whole time. Stand still until I say go. Bend, then
jump as high as you can. Land softly on both feet and stand back up still." Do not coach jump
strategy (how deep to dip, how fast). The strategy is what we are measuring.

## Testing protocol

For each athlete in the queue:

1. **Starting position.** Normal standing posture on the plates, one foot on each plate.
   Hands on hips. Chest up, eyes forward. (If a weighted jump is prescribed, hands on the
   barbell instead; that is a different test and is not covered here.)
2. **Weigh.** Click Weigh Athlete. The athlete must be completely still. Do not accept body
   weight until the display registers green.
3. **Stabilize.** The athlete stays completely still for 2 to 3 seconds before the first
   jump and between jumps.
4. **Start recording.** Click Start Recording.
5. **Jump.** Cue "go." The athlete bends, jumps as high as possible, lands softly on both
   feet, and returns to the starting position.
6. **Repeat** for a total of 3 countermovement jumps, with the 2 to 3 second still pause
   between each.
7. **Stop recording.** Click Stop Recording.
8. **Analyze and save.** Click Analyze and Save. Review the reps (next section) before you
   confirm. Apply the session tag [CONFIRM: tag convention, for example sport, session type,
   in-season or off-season].
9. **Next athlete.** Select the next profile in the queue and repeat from step 1.

Time per athlete: about 90 seconds. A squad of 16 takes about 25 minutes with one plate set.

## Data quality checks

Check these before you save. A rep that fails any of them is discarded and repeated, not
saved and explained later.

| Check | What good looks like | If not |
|---|---|---|
| Weigh-in | Display registered green; body weight within about 1 kg of the athlete's last reading | Re-weigh. If body weight is off by more than 2 kg, confirm it is the right profile |
| Stillness | Flat force trace before the jump; the app finds the start of movement cleanly | Have the athlete reset and hold still longer. Talking and shifting weight both show up |
| Hands | On hips from start to landing | Discard the rep. Arm swing adds height and changes the strategy metrics |
| Feet | Both feet on their own plate at takeoff and landing; no shuffle, no step off | Discard the rep. A foot that lands off a plate breaks the asymmetry numbers |
| Effort | Three reps within a few centimeters of each other | A single low rep is usually a poor effort. One retest is fine. Two low reps may be real; keep them and note it |
| Landing | Soft, both feet, standing still afterward | A hard, stiff landing is not an error for the takeoff metrics, but note that Baylor's protocol cues soft, so landing force metrics are not comparable to protocols that cue stiff |
| Count | Exactly 3 CMJ reps detected | If the app found 2 or 4, check whether a reset bounce was read as a jump; delete the extra or re-run |
| Profile | The right athlete | Wrong profile is the most expensive error. Fix it before saving, not in the database later |

Reading the first numbers: jump height uses the impulse-momentum method
(Jump Height, Imp-Mom), not flight time, because flight time is inflated by a tucked
landing. RSI-modified is jump height divided by contraction time. Asymmetry is
(left minus right) divided by the larger of the two, as a percentage. All three definitions
are in the Operations Guide glossary. [CONFIRM: that Imp-Mom is the jump height variant in
Baylor reports.]

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Plates will not connect to the app | Cable loose, plates not powered, app on the wrong device | Reseat both cable ends, power cycle the plates, restart the app. [CONFIRM: whether Baylor's plates connect by USB or Bluetooth] |
| Weigh-in never turns green | Athlete moving, plate rocking on uneven floor, something touching a plate | Still the athlete, move to a flatter spot, clear the plates and re-zero |
| App finds the wrong number of reps | Reset bounce read as a jump, or the stabilize pause was too short | Delete the extra rep in review, or re-run with a longer still pause |
| Left and right look swapped | Platform Assignment setting does not match the physical layout | Fix the setting before testing anyone else. Flag any sessions recorded with it wrong |
| Numbers look off for one athlete | Wrong profile, wrong body weight, or arms came off hips | Check the profile and weight first. Review the video or ask the spotter |
| Test will not save or export | Export folder missing or disconnected; cloud sync not signed in | Check the Auto Test Export Folder path and the VALD Hub login. Data stays on the device until sync succeeds; do not clear it |
| App freezes | Memory, or too many profiles in one recording | Close and restart the app. Keep recordings to one squad |
| Battery or power lost mid-session | [CONFIRM: whether plates are battery or mains powered] | Saved reps are kept. Re-run the athlete who was on the plates |

Vendor support: VALD support through the Hub help menu [CONFIRM: Baylor's VALD account
contact, and the vendor support hours]. Do not share athlete data in a support ticket;
describe the problem and send screenshots with names removed.

## Data management and export

Where the data goes, in order:

1. **ForceDecks app** on the testing device. The raw force traces and the computed metrics.
2. **VALD Hub** (cloud). Syncs from the app when the device is online. This is where staff
   view results and build reports. [CONFIRM: that sync is automatic on this device.]
3. **Kitman Labs.** The athlete management system of record. [CONFIRM: whether the VALD to
   Kitman integration is live for all sports, or whether ForceDecks data reaches Kitman by
   CSV or not at all.]
4. **Department database.** The force plate decision system and the CMJ traffic light pull
   from VALD by API or CSV export into a local DuckDB database for the Wednesday read.
   [CONFIRM: which one is the current path, and who runs it.]

**File naming** for any manual export, from the SOP template:
`YYYY-MM-DD_SportCode_TestType_AthleteID`, for example `2026-10-23_WVB_CMJ_1234`.
Use the athlete ID, not the name, in file names. [CONFIRM: the ID source and the sport code
list.]

**After every session:**

- Confirm the session appears in VALD Hub with the right date, sport tag and athlete count.
- If a rep was discarded and re-run, the discarded rep should not be in Hub.
- Note anything unusual (fatigue, shoes, a late arrival) in the session note, not in a text
  message.

**Who may see what.** CMJ results are performance data, not health data, under the draft
NCAA guide's classification. They go to the athlete, the Athletic Performance coach, the sport
coach through the agreed report, and Athletic Medicine when return-to-play is involved.
Identifiable results never go into email to outside parties, personal cloud storage, code
repositories or unapproved AI tools. The full rules are the guide's section 4 and the
Digest's Part 3.

**Retention.** [CONFIRM: how long raw traces are kept on the device and in Hub; the NCAA
guide leaves the retention period pending General Counsel.]

## Teardown and storage

1. Stop recording and confirm the last save.
2. Confirm sync to VALD Hub if the device is online; if not, sync as soon as it is.
3. Power down the plates and the device.
4. Disconnect cables; coil, do not bend at the connector.
5. Wipe the plate surfaces.
6. Return everything to the case in its labeled spot and the case to its storage location
   [CONFIRM: location]. Put the device on charge.

## Who to contact

| Question | Contact |
|---|---|
| The protocol, cues, or whether to postpone a test | Director of Applied Performance |
| Running the test day to day, equipment location | [CONFIRM: Associate Director of Applied Performance or the daily user named above] |
| An athlete returning from injury | Athletic Medicine staff for that sport, then the Director |
| App, plates, Hub login | Vendor support through VALD Hub; then the Director |
| Data in the department database or the Wednesday read | [CONFIRM: owner of the force plate decision system] |

Phone numbers and emails live in the Digest appendix contact table, not here, so a staff
change does not orphan this chapter.

## Revision history

| Date | Author | Change | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-04 | Drafted for Eric Rash | First draft from the V3 protocol, the Operations Guide ForceDecks section, the SOP template, and the Iowa manual's format | 0.1 |

## Open questions for Eric

Answer these before the 10/23 ship date. Each one is also a [CONFIRM] tag above.

1. **Is V3 the live protocol?** Memory marks the Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol as
   "author uncertain." Is it what the staff run today, and is 3 reps still the count?
2. **Which ForceDecks app version is on the testing device?** The Operations Guide and V3
   use different button names. The chapter should match the screen.
3. **Soft landing or stiff landing?** V3 cues soft. Iowa cues stiff to read peak landing
   force. Soft is safer and matches practice, but it means landing-phase metrics are not
   comparable to published stiff-landing data. Keep soft and say so, or change?
4. **Who is the daily user and co-owner of this chapter?** The ship rule needs a named
   person who will run it, mark it up, and answer the 30-day check on 11/22.
5. **Which metrics are reported** for daily readiness and for coach reports, and is Jump
   Height (Imp-Mom) the variant in use?
6. **What is the live data path** from VALD Hub to Kitman Labs and to the department
   database? Which sports have the integration?
7. **Equipment facts:** plate model and serials, testing device name, storage location,
   vault name, sport code list, athlete ID source.
8. **Does this chapter replace the ForceDecks section of the Operations Guide** once it
   ships, or do both stand until the Digest covers all of Part 2?

  path, and whether the auto export is still used now that data goes to VALD Hub]

Note on app versions. The Operations Guide describes buttons called Weigh Start and Play.
Baylor's Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol describes Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and
Analyze and Save. These are two different versions of the ForceDecks software. This chapter
uses the V3 names. [CONFIRM: which version is installed on the testing device, and update
the button names to match.]

### Build the queue

Double-click profile names to add the athletes you are testing to the queue. Up to 16
profiles can be tested in one recording. If an athlete is new, create the profile first
[CONFIRM: naming convention for profiles, and whether the roster syncs from Kitman Labs or
is entered by hand].

### Zero the plates

Click Play (or Start). Make sure nothing is touching the plates, then let them zero. If a
cable, a shoe or a hand is on a plate during zeroing, every number that follows is wrong.

## Preparing the athlete

### Two testing conditions

**Condition 1: inside a training session.** The team warm-up is the warm-up. Test at the
same point in the session every time [CONFIRM: for example right after the warm-up and
before the first lift].

**Condition 2: outside a training session.** Run the standard warm-up from the V3 protocol:

- Line hops, forward and backward then left and right, 10 each
- Open gate and close gate (hip internal and external rotation), 5 each
- Rapid squat to stand (triple extension), 5

### Rules that keep the numbers comparable

These are the rules the handbook chapter "Preparing the athlete for a test" will carry. Until
it ships, they live here. They matter most for Condition 2 and for any test used before and
after a training phase. For daily readiness jumps inside a session, apply what you can and
note anything unusual.

- Same time of day as the athlete's previous tests, within reason.
- No food or caffeine in the two hours before a planned test.
- No hard session in the 48 hours before a planned test. If an athlete arrives obviously
  fatigued or sore, record the jump as a readiness data point but do not treat it as a
  baseline or a phase test. If it is a phase test, postpone it.
- Shoes: the same type the athlete trained in last time. Note a change.
- New athletes get at least three familiarization trials before their first recorded
  session. Someone who is still being coached through the movement will improve next time
  just from learning it, and that looks like a training effect.

### Explain the test

Tell the athlete: "Hands on your hips the whole time. Stand still until I say go. Bend, then
jump as high as you can. Land softly on both feet and stand back up still." Do not coach jump
strategy (how deep to dip, how fast). The strategy is what we are measuring.

## Testing protocol

For each athlete in the queue:

1. **Starting position.** Normal standing posture on the plates, one foot on each plate.
   Hands on hips. Chest up, eyes forward. (If a weighted jump is prescribed, hands on the
   barbell instead; that is a different test and is not covered here.)
2. **Weigh.** Click Weigh Athlete. The athlete must be completely still. Do not accept body
   weight until the display registers green.
3. **Stabilize.** The athlete stays completely still for 2 to 3 seconds before the first
   jump and between jumps.
4. **Start recording.** Click Start Recording.
5. **Jump.** Cue "go." The athlete bends, jumps as high as possible, lands softly on both
   feet, and returns to the starting position.
6. **Repeat** for a total of 3 countermovement jumps, with the 2 to 3 second still pause
   between each.
7. **Stop recording.** Click Stop Recording.
8. **Analyze and save.** Click Analyze and Save. Review the reps (next section) before you
   confirm. Apply the session tag [CONFIRM: tag convention, for example sport, session type,
   in-season or off-season].
9. **Next athlete.** Select the next profile in the queue and repeat from step 1.

Time per athlete: about 90 seconds. A squad of 16 takes about 25 minutes with one plate set.

## Data quality checks

Check these before you save. A rep that fails any of them is discarded and repeated, not
saved and explained later.

| Check | What good looks like | If not |
|---|---|---|
| Weigh-in | Display registered green; body weight within about 1 kg of the athlete's last reading | Re-weigh. If body weight is off by more than 2 kg, confirm it is the right profile |
| Stillness | Flat force trace before the jump; the app finds the start of movement cleanly | Have the athlete reset and hold still longer. Talking and shifting weight both show up |
| Hands | On hips from start to landing | Discard the rep. Arm swing adds height and changes the strategy metrics |
| Feet | Both feet on their own plate at takeoff and landing; no shuffle, no step off | Discard the rep. A foot that lands off a plate breaks the asymmetry numbers |
| Effort | Three reps within a few centimeters of each other | A single low rep is usually a poor effort. One retest is fine. Two low reps may be real; keep them and note it |
| Landing | Soft, both feet, standing still afterward | A hard, stiff landing is not an error for the takeoff metrics, but note that Baylor's protocol cues soft, so landing force metrics are not comparable to protocols that cue stiff |
| Count | Exactly 3 CMJ reps detected | If the app found 2 or 4, check whether a reset bounce was read as a jump; delete the extra or re-run |
| Profile | The right athlete | Wrong profile is the most expensive error. Fix it before saving, not in the database later |

Reading the first numbers: jump height uses the impulse-momentum method
(Jump Height, Imp-Mom), not flight time, because flight time is inflated by a tucked
landing. RSI-modified is jump height divided by contraction time. Asymmetry is
(left minus right) divided by the larger of the two, as a percentage. All three definitions
are in the Operations Guide glossary. [CONFIRM: that Imp-Mom is the jump height variant in
Baylor reports.]

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Plates will not connect to the app | Cable loose, plates not powered, app on the wrong device | Reseat both cable ends, power cycle the plates, restart the app. [CONFIRM: whether Baylor's plates connect by USB or Bluetooth] |
| Weigh-in never turns green | Athlete moving, plate rocking on uneven floor, something touching a plate | Still the athlete, move to a flatter spot, clear the plates and re-zero |
| App finds the wrong number of reps | Reset bounce read as a jump, or the stabilize pause was too short | Delete the extra rep in review, or re-run with a longer still pause |
| Left and right look swapped | Platform Assignment setting does not match the physical layout | Fix the setting before testing anyone else. Flag any sessions recorded with it wrong |
| Numbers look off for one athlete | Wrong profile, wrong body weight, or arms came off hips | Check the profile and weight first. Review the video or ask the spotter |
| Test will not save or export | Export folder missing or disconnected; cloud sync not signed in | Check the Auto Test Export Folder path and the VALD Hub login. Data stays on the device until sync succeeds; do not clear it |
| App freezes | Memory, or too many profiles in one recording | Close and restart the app. Keep recordings to one squad |
| Battery or power lost mid-session | [CONFIRM: whether plates are battery or mains powered] | Saved reps are kept. Re-run the athlete who was on the plates |

Vendor support: VALD support through the Hub help menu [CONFIRM: Baylor's VALD account
contact, and the vendor support hours]. Do not share athlete data in a support ticket;
describe the problem and send screenshots with names removed.

## Data management and export

Where the data goes, in order:

1. **ForceDecks app** on the testing device. The raw force traces and the computed metrics.
2. **VALD Hub** (cloud). Syncs from the app when the device is online. This is where staff
   view results and build reports. [CONFIRM: that sync is automatic on this device.]
3. **Kitman Labs.** The athlete management system of record. [CONFIRM: whether the VALD to
   Kitman integration is live for all sports, or whether ForceDecks data reaches Kitman by
   CSV or not at all.]
4. **Department database.** The force plate decision system and the CMJ traffic light pull
   from VALD by API or CSV export into a local DuckDB database for the Wednesday read.
   [CONFIRM: which one is the current path, and who runs it.]

**File naming** for any manual export, from the SOP template:
`YYYY-MM-DD_SportCode_TestType_AthleteID`, for example `2026-10-23_WVB_CMJ_1234`.
Use the athlete ID, not the name, in file names. [CONFIRM: the ID source and the sport code
list.]

**After every session:**

- Confirm the session appears in VALD Hub with the right date, sport tag and athlete count.
- If a rep was discarded and re-run, the discarded rep should not be in Hub.
- Note anything unusual (fatigue, shoes, a late arrival) in the session note, not in a text
  message.

**Who may see what.** CMJ results are performance data, not health data, under the draft
NCAA guide's classification. They go to the athlete, the Athletic Performance coach, the sport
coach through the agreed report, and Athletic Medicine when return-to-play is involved.
Identifiable results never go into email to outside parties, personal cloud storage, code
repositories or unapproved AI tools. The full rules are the guide's section 4 and the
Digest's Part 3.

**Retention.** [CONFIRM: how long raw traces are kept on the device and in Hub; the NCAA
guide leaves the retention period pending General Counsel.]

## Teardown and storage

1. Stop recording and confirm the last save.
2. Confirm sync to VALD Hub if the device is online; if not, sync as soon as it is.
3. Power down the plates and the device.
4. Disconnect cables; coil, do not bend at the connector.
5. Wipe the plate surfaces.
6. Return everything to the case in its labeled spot and the case to its storage location
   [CONFIRM: location]. Put the device on charge.

## Who to contact

| Question | Contact |
|---|---|
| The protocol, cues, or whether to postpone a test | Director of Applied Performance |
| Running the test day to day, equipment location | [CONFIRM: Associate Director of Applied Performance or the daily user named above] |
| An athlete returning from injury | Athletic Medicine staff for that sport, then the Director |
| App, plates, Hub login | Vendor support through VALD Hub; then the Director |
| Data in the department database or the Wednesday read | [CONFIRM: owner of the force plate decision system] |

Phone numbers and emails live in the Digest appendix contact table, not here, so a staff
change does not orphan this chapter.

## Revision history

| Date | Author | Change | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-04 | Drafted for Eric Rash | First draft from the V3 protocol, the Operations Guide ForceDecks section, the SOP template, and the Iowa manual's format | 0.1 |

## Open questions for Eric

Answer these before the 10/23 ship date. Each one is also a [CONFIRM] tag above.

1. **Is V3 the live protocol?** Memory marks the Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol as
   "author uncertain." Is it what the staff run today, and is 3 reps still the count?
2. **Which ForceDecks app version is on the testing device?** The Operations Guide and V3
   use different button names. The chapter should match the screen.
3. **Soft landing or stiff landing?** V3 cues soft. Iowa cues stiff to read peak landing
   force. Soft is safer and matches practice, but it means landing-phase metrics are not
   comparable to published stiff-landing data. Keep soft and say so, or change?
4. **Who is the daily user and co-owner of this chapter?** The ship rule needs a named
   person who will run it, mark it up, and answer the 30-day check on 11/22.
5. **Which metrics are reported** for daily readiness and for coach reports, and is Jump
   Height (Imp-Mom) the variant in use?
6. **What is the live data path** from VALD Hub to Kitman Labs and to the department
   database? Which sports have the integration?
7. **Equipment facts:** plate model and serials, testing device name, storage location,
   vault name, sport code list, athlete ID source.
8. **Does this chapter replace the ForceDecks section of the Operations Guide** once it
   ships, or do both stand until the Digest covers all of Part 2?

# Gap update: what the Feb 2026 plan still gets right, what changed, and the Iowa column

Written 2026-10-04. Builds on `Performance_Playbook_Development_Plan.docx` (Feb 2026,
Clemson vs Baylor). This does not redo that analysis. It checks it against the current
Baylor document, records what changed around it, and adds the comparison it lacked: Iowa.

## Short answer

The Feb 2026 plan still holds in full, because the Baylor document it analyzed has not
changed. The Nov 2025 docx is the May 2024 text with a few formatting edits (97.5 percent
identical at word level). What changed is everything around the document: the NCAA SSI
recommendations and Baylor's draft response to them, the two-week ship rule, the intern
curriculum becoming its own project, and one workflow (NordBord) that no longer matches
practice. Iowa adds one thing neither Clemson nor Baylor has: a written theory of testing
and a fixed per-test format that a coach can read without a software manual.

## What the Feb 2026 plan still gets right

1. **The five gap categories.** No intern curriculum, no sport-specific data dictionaries,
   no daily checklists or accountability, generic template workflows, no principles or
   policies. All five are still open. None of the Phase 1, 2 or 3 actions were carried out.
2. **The strengths list.** Baylor's institutional framing (Preparing Champions for Life,
   One Standard One Accord) and the Health and Wellness placement are an identity Clemson
   lacks. The ForceDecks and Perch metric glossaries are deeper than Clemson's. Keep all of
   it in the handbook.
3. **The diagnosis of the workflows.** Only Catapult reads like it was written from
   practice. The VALD, Perch, Polar and SmartSpeed workflows follow one generic template with
   no device names, storage locations or troubleshooting. Still true, and chapter 1 is the
   first fix.
4. **Keep credentials out of the document.** Baylor's placeholder approach was right.
   Clemson listed passwords in plain text. The plan's fix (a credential vault, referenced not
   printed) stands and now also satisfies the NCAA guide's section 6 on institutional admin
   accounts.
5. **The 14-section final structure.** Still the right content list. The Digest regroups it
   under three parts (handbook, ops manual, NCAA tech items) and adds four chapters; see
   `outline.md`.
6. **Keep the intern curriculum separate** (plan section 5.3). Confirmed: it is now the
   `Intern_Curriculum` project with its own 10/9 deadline. The Digest references it.
7. **Pilot sport-specific data dictionaries with 2 or 3 sports** (plan section 7). Still the
   right approach; not started.

## What has changed since February

| Change | Effect on the Digest |
|---|---|
| **NCAA SSI recommendations (March 2026) and Baylor's Draft v1 response (Oct 4).** Nine-page guide plus five forms covering governance, adoption, consent, data management, vendor contracts, staff transitions and annual review. | Becomes Part 3 of the Digest by link. Not in the Feb plan at all. The guide waits on three decisions from Chris Ruf by 10/14, so Part 3 stays a link until then. |
| **The ship rule (D1, 2026-09-25).** One piece every two weeks to a named user, logged in the status report, 30-day stick check. The self-audit found that the one change that stuck had a daily-user co-owner. | The Digest ships one chapter at a time, in ship order, each with a named user. The Feb plan's three 4-to-6-week phases are replaced by a chapter queue. Chapter 1 (ForceDecks CMJ) is due 10/23. |
| **Intern curriculum became its own project** with Module 1 due 10/9. Eric confirmed on 2026-09-28 that it "has not been built yet." | Part 1 of the Digest gets a short "interns and graduate assistants" chapter that points to the curriculum. The 16-week table in the Feb plan moves to that project. |
| **NordBord practice changed.** Roster-wide football NordBord testing was retired after January 2023; it is kept for small return-to-play groups with Athletic Medicine. The Operations Guide still documents the full roster SOP. | The NordBord chapter must document current practice and the decision rule behind it (small numbers, clear clinical purpose, dedicated oversight). The Feb plan did not catch this. |
| **Baylor's CMJ practice is now written down in memory.** Daily CMJ builds the baseline; modified RSI is read on Wednesdays against individualized thresholds; DSI steers training emphasis. The Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol gives Baylor's own scripted steps. | Chapter 1 has a Baylor source to write from, not just a vendor template. The Feb plan assumed workflows would have to be written fresh. |
| **The department pulls ForceDecks data into its own database** (DuckDB via CSV export or the VALD API) for the traffic-light and decision-system projects. | The data management chapter can describe a real pipeline: ForceDecks to VALD Hub to local database to reports, with Kitman Labs as the athlete management system. |
| **Leadership preference recorded (2026-07-30):** flexible best-practice documents over rigid formal policy. | The handbook's policies chapter is written as expectations with examples, not rules with penalties. Clemson's termination language is not borrowed. |
| **Staff terms fixed.** Athletic Performance (not S&C), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science). | The Feb plan uses "S&C" and "sport science" throughout; the Digest translates. The Baylor guide itself says "Athletics Performance" (with an s); see open questions. |

## The Iowa column

Iowa's manual is a different kind of document. Clemson and Baylor are technology playbooks
organized by device. Iowa is an assessment manual organized by physical quality (jump,
strength, endurance, speed), written for Athletic Performance coaches, with almost no
software steps. That is why it fills gaps the other two share.

| Dimension | Clemson (2023) | Baylor (current) | Iowa (2017) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Why we test | Six principles, narrative | Four principles, bullets | A quoted purpose statement, then specific vs general tests explained with an example |
| Test theory | None | None | Validity (seven types), reliability (interrater, intrarater), learning effect, detecting change, smallest meaningful change |
| When to test again | None | None | Three factors: phase of season, expected change, known fatigue. Plus menstrual cycle considerations |
| Athlete preparation | None | None | Standard rules: carbohydrate 36 h out, no food or caffeine 2 h before, no heavy fatigue 48 to 72 h before, same time of day, fixed test order |
| Per-test format | Setup, testing, troubleshooting, data management, links | Preparation, registration, calibration, protocol, positioning, test, data, feedback, post-test, export (template) | Description, how to test, frequency by purpose, validity and reliability, interpretation with numbers, equipment |
| Frequency guidance | None | None | Per metric and per purpose (asymmetry monthly; jump height weekly as a 3-jump average; RSImod weekly in season; DSI before and after phases) |
| Interpretation bands | None | None | DSI 0.6 and 0.8 cutoffs; RSA decrement 2 to 10 percent; sprint splits as acceleration, speed, combined, momentum |
| Audience | Interns | Staff and interns (implicitly) | Athletic Performance coaches, with a standing offer of help from the performance staff |
| Software steps | Detailed, by device | Detailed for Catapult; template for the rest | None |
| Troubleshooting | Every device | None | None |
| Daily checklist | Device by device, AM and PM | None | None |
| Data dictionary | By sport | By vendor | None |
| Credentials | Printed in plain text | Placeholders | None |

### What Iowa does that Baylor and Clemson do not

1. **Explains why before how.** Three pages on validity, reliability and detecting change
   before any test appears. A new intern or a coach reading it learns what a 3-jump average
   is for and why one jump is not enough.
2. **Standardizes the athlete, not just the device.** Diet, caffeine, fatigue window, time
   of day, test order. Clemson and Baylor standardize the hardware and software and leave the
   athlete's state uncontrolled. This is the single biggest gain for data quality.
3. **States frequency by purpose.** The same CMJ is weekly for fatigue monitoring, monthly
   for asymmetry, and before and after a phase for DSI. Baylor's practice does this (daily
   jumps, Wednesday read) but has never written it down.
4. **Gives numbers to interpret against.** Cutoffs, ratios and formulas in the text, with a
   warning that they are guidelines, not rules.
5. **Tells the reader when not to test.** Known fatigue, wrong time in the season, an
   athlete whose readiness does not match the assessment. Postpone.
6. **Writes for the coach.** Plain sentences, no vendor language, and a repeated line that
   the performance staff will help with the parts beyond the manual.

### Iowa's limits

- The stack is 2017: GymAware, contact mats, FreeLap, MyJump. None of the device steps
  transfer.
- No software steps, no troubleshooting, no data management, no file naming. It cannot
  stand alone as an ops manual.
- Some Frequency sections are empty and the sport assessment table is an image.
- Its CMJ cue is a stiff landing to read peak landing force. Baylor's V3 protocol cues a
  soft landing. The Digest follows Baylor and flags the trade-off (see chapter 1 open
  questions).
- It names a staff member as the contact for two tests. The Digest uses roles, not names,
  in any text that outlives a staff change.

## What this means for the Digest

- **Part 1 (handbook) gains two Iowa-derived chapters:** "Why we test" (assessment
  principles) and the athlete preparation standards that every ops-manual chapter points to.
- **Every ops-manual chapter follows a merged format:** Iowa's front half (description,
  frequency by purpose, interpretation) plus the SOP template's back half (setup, software
  steps, data quality, troubleshooting, export, contacts). Chapter 1 is the first instance.
- **Part 3 (NCAA) is link-only** until Chris Ruf's 10/14 decisions, then a one-page staff
  summary per section.
- **The Feb plan's phases become a chapter queue** ordered by who is waiting for what. See
  `outline.md` for priorities.

## Open questions this update raises

1. The Baylor guide says "Athletics Performance." The Digest's term list says "Athletic
   Performance." Which is the department's official name on the org chart?
2. Does the Digest retire the Operations Guide docx, or do both live until the Digest covers
   every section?
3. Who co-owns each ops-manual chapter as its daily user? The D1 finding says a chapter
   without one will fade.

# Chapter 1: ForceDecks countermovement jump procedure

**DRAFT 0.1, 2026-10-04. Not yet run by a named user. Items marked [CONFIRM: ...] are
Baylor facts the author could not verify. Do not ship until they are resolved.**

Part 2, Ops manual. Applied Performance Digest.

| Owner | Daily user | Last reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| Director of Applied Performance | [CONFIRM: name and role of the staff member or intern who runs CMJ testing most days] | 2026-10-04 (draft) |

## The short version

Three countermovement jumps on the ForceDecks, hands on hips, after a weigh-in that reads
green. The athlete stands still, bends, jumps as high as they can, lands softly, and resets.
You review the three reps before you save. The whole thing takes about 90 seconds per athlete
once the plates are up.

## What this test is for

The countermovement jump (CMJ) is the test Applied Performance runs most, and it does three
jobs:

1. **Daily readiness.** Jumps during the week build each athlete's baseline. Modified
   reactive strength index (RSI-modified) is read against that baseline on Wednesdays, using
   percent change, a rolling average, and the smallest worthwhile change to tell a real drop
   from noise. Thresholds are individual, not one number for the team.
2. **Asymmetry.** Left and right plate forces show whether an athlete is loading one side
   more than the other. Useful monthly, and more often for an athlete returning from injury
   with Athletic Medicine.
3. **Training emphasis.** CMJ peak force divided by isometric mid-thigh pull peak force
   gives the dynamic strength index, which helps decide between more plyometric work and
   more maximal strength work. That needs the mid-thigh pull too; see chapter O5.

Because the same test serves three purposes, the procedure has to be the same every time.
A test can keep its name while the cue, the rep count or a software setting changes
underneath it, and the data will not tell you. That is why this chapter fixes all three in
writing.

**How often.** Daily or near-daily during training blocks for the readiness baseline
[CONFIRM: which sports jump daily, and which jump weekly]. Monthly asymmetry review.
Before and after a training phase for the dynamic strength index.

**What we report.** Pick a few metrics and keep them. The working rule is one or two output
metrics (jump height), one to three driver metrics (concentric impulse, eccentric braking
force), one to three strategy metrics (contraction time, countermovement depth), and
left-right asymmetry where it matters. Add anything else only with a reason written down.
[CONFIRM: the current reported metric set for daily readiness and for coach reports.]

## Setup

### Equipment

1. ForceDecks dual force plates [CONFIRM: model, serial numbers]
2. Laptop or tablet with the ForceDecks app [CONFIRM: device name and which app version, see note below]
3. Plate cables and power supply
4. Carrying case [CONFIRM: storage location, room and shelf]

Photo to add: full kit laid out and labeled.

### Location

A flat, hard, level floor with room for the athlete to jump and land without stepping off.
Rubber flooring is fine if the plates sit flat and do not rock. Near an outlet if the session
will run long.

Recommended locations: [CONFIRM: for example the main weight room, the Athletic Medicine
space, or a sport-specific facility].

### Software settings

Log in to the ForceDecks app with the department account. Credentials are in the vault, not
in this document. [CONFIRM: vault name and who has access.]

Confirm these settings before the first athlete steps on. They are the ones the current
Operations Guide lists:

- Layout, Operational Mode: Shared
- Layout, Show Profile Selection Pane: Always
- Platforms, Sequenced Platform Count: 1
- Platforms, Platform Assignment: matches the physical left and right plates
- Platforms, Auto Test Export Folder: the same folder as ForceDecks [CONFIRM: exact folder
  path, and whether the auto export is still used now that data goes to VALD Hub]

Note on app versions. The Operations Guide describes buttons called Weigh Start and Play.
Baylor's Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol describes Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and
Analyze and Save. These are two different versions of the ForceDecks software. This chapter
uses the V3 names. [CONFIRM: which version is installed on the testing device, and update
the button names to match.]

### Build the queue

Double-click profile names to add the athletes you are testing to the queue. Up to 16
profiles can be tested in one recording. If an athlete is new, create the profile first
[CONFIRM: naming convention for profiles, and whether the roster syncs from Kitman Labs or
is entered by hand].

### Zero the plates

Click Play (or Start). Make sure nothing is touching the plates, then let them zero. If a
cable, a shoe or a hand is on a plate during zeroing, every number that follows is wrong.

## Preparing the athlete

### Two testing conditions

**Condition 1: inside a training session.** The team warm-up is the warm-up. Test at the
same point in the session every time [CONFIRM: for example right after the warm-up and
before the first lift].

**Condition 2: outside a training session.** Run the standard warm-up from the V3 protocol:

- Line hops, forward and backward then left and right, 10 each
- Open gate and close gate (hip internal and external rotation), 5 each
- Rapid squat to stand (triple extension), 5

### Rules that keep the numbers comparable

These are the rules the handbook chapter "Preparing the athlete for a test" will carry. Until
it ships, they live here. They matter most for Condition 2 and for any test used before and
after a training phase. For daily readiness jumps inside a session, apply what you can and
note anything unusual.

- Same time of day as the athlete's previous tests, within reason.
- No food or caffeine in the two hours before a planned test.
- No hard session in the 48 hours before a planned test. If an athlete arrives obviously
  fatigued or sore, record the jump as a readiness data point but do not treat it as a
  baseline or a phase test. If it is a phase test, postpone it.
- Shoes: the same type the athlete trained in last time. Note a change.
- New athletes get at least three familiarization trials before their first recorded
  session. Someone who is still being coached through the movement will improve next time
  just from learning it, and that looks like a training effect.

### Explain the test

Tell the athlete: "Hands on your hips the whole time. Stand still until I say go. Bend, then
jump as high as you can. Land softly on both feet and stand back up still." Do not coach jump
strategy (how deep to dip, how fast). The strategy is what we are measuring.

## Testing protocol

For each athlete in the queue:

1. **Starting position.** Normal standing posture on the plates, one foot on each plate.
   Hands on hips. Chest up, eyes forward. (If a weighted jump is prescribed, hands on the
   barbell instead; that is a different test and is not covered here.)
2. **Weigh.** Click Weigh Athlete. The athlete must be completely still. Do not accept body
   weight until the display registers green.
3. **Stabilize.** The athlete stays completely still for 2 to 3 seconds before the first
   jump and between jumps.
4. **Start recording.** Click Start Recording.
5. **Jump.** Cue "go." The athlete bends, jumps as high as possible, lands softly on both
   feet, and returns to the starting position.
6. **Repeat** for a total of 3 countermovement jumps, with the 2 to 3 second still pause
   between each.
7. **Stop recording.** Click Stop Recording.
8. **Analyze and save.** Click Analyze and Save. Review the reps (next section) before you
   confirm. Apply the session tag [CONFIRM: tag convention, for example sport, session type,
   in-season or off-season].
9. **Next athlete.** Select the next profile in the queue and repeat from step 1.

Time per athlete: about 90 seconds. A squad of 16 takes about 25 minutes with one plate set.

## Data quality checks

Check these before you save. A rep that fails any of them is discarded and repeated, not
saved and explained later.

| Check | What good looks like | If not |
|---|---|---|
| Weigh-in | Display registered green; body weight within about 1 kg of the athlete's last reading | Re-weigh. If body weight is off by more than 2 kg, confirm it is the right profile |
| Stillness | Flat force trace before the jump; the app finds the start of movement cleanly | Have the athlete reset and hold still longer. Talking and shifting weight both show up |
| Hands | On hips from start to landing | Discard the rep. Arm swing adds height and changes the strategy metrics |
| Feet | Both feet on their own plate at takeoff and landing; no shuffle, no step off | Discard the rep. A foot that lands off a plate breaks the asymmetry numbers |
| Effort | Three reps within a few centimeters of each other | A single low rep is usually a poor effort. One retest is fine. Two low reps may be real; keep them and note it |
| Landing | Soft, both feet, standing still afterward | A hard, stiff landing is not an error for the takeoff metrics, but note that Baylor's protocol cues soft, so landing force metrics are not comparable to protocols that cue stiff |
| Count | Exactly 3 CMJ reps detected | If the app found 2 or 4, check whether a reset bounce was read as a jump; delete the extra or re-run |
| Profile | The right athlete | Wrong profile is the most expensive error. Fix it before saving, not in the database later |

Reading the first numbers: jump height uses the impulse-momentum method
(Jump Height, Imp-Mom), not flight time, because flight time is inflated by a tucked
landing. RSI-modified is jump height divided by contraction time. Asymmetry is
(left minus right) divided by the larger of the two, as a percentage. All three definitions
are in the Operations Guide glossary. [CONFIRM: that Imp-Mom is the jump height variant in
Baylor reports.]

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Plates will not connect to the app | Cable loose, plates not powered, app on the wrong device | Reseat both cable ends, power cycle the plates, restart the app. [CONFIRM: whether Baylor's plates connect by USB or Bluetooth] |
| Weigh-in never turns green | Athlete moving, plate rocking on uneven floor, something touching a plate | Still the athlete, move to a flatter spot, clear the plates and re-zero |
| App finds the wrong number of reps | Reset bounce read as a jump, or the stabilize pause was too short | Delete the extra rep in review, or re-run with a longer still pause |
| Left and right look swapped | Platform Assignment setting does not match the physical layout | Fix the setting before testing anyone else. Flag any sessions recorded with it wrong |
| Numbers look off for one athlete | Wrong profile, wrong body weight, or arms came off hips | Check the profile and weight first. Review the video or ask the spotter |
| Test will not save or export | Export folder missing or disconnected; cloud sync not signed in | Check the Auto Test Export Folder path and the VALD Hub login. Data stays on the device until sync succeeds; do not clear it |
| App freezes | Memory, or too many profiles in one recording | Close and restart the app. Keep recordings to one squad |
| Battery or power lost mid-session | [CONFIRM: whether plates are battery or mains powered] | Saved reps are kept. Re-run the athlete who was on the plates |

Vendor support: VALD support through the Hub help menu [CONFIRM: Baylor's VALD account
contact, and the vendor support hours]. Do not share athlete data in a support ticket;
describe the problem and send screenshots with names removed.

## Data management and export

Where the data goes, in order:

1. **ForceDecks app** on the testing device. The raw force traces and the computed metrics.
2. **VALD Hub** (cloud). Syncs from the app when the device is online. This is where staff
   view results and build reports. [CONFIRM: that sync is automatic on this device.]
3. **Kitman Labs.** The athlete management system of record. [CONFIRM: whether the VALD to
   Kitman integration is live for all sports, or whether ForceDecks data reaches Kitman by
   CSV or not at all.]
4. **Department database.** The force plate decision system and the CMJ traffic light pull
   from VALD by API or CSV export into a local DuckDB database for the Wednesday read.
   [CONFIRM: which one is the current path, and who runs it.]

**File naming** for any manual export, from the SOP template:
`YYYY-MM-DD_SportCode_TestType_AthleteID`, for example `2026-10-23_WVB_CMJ_1234`.
Use the athlete ID, not the name, in file names. [CONFIRM: the ID source and the sport code
list.]

**After every session:**

- Confirm the session appears in VALD Hub with the right date, sport tag and athlete count.
- If a rep was discarded and re-run, the discarded rep should not be in Hub.
- Note anything unusual (fatigue, shoes, a late arrival) in the session note, not in a text
  message.

**Who may see what.** CMJ results are performance data, not health data, under the draft
NCAA guide's classification. They go to the athlete, the Athletic Performance coach, the sport
coach through the agreed report, and Athletic Medicine when return-to-play is involved.
Identifiable results never go into email to outside parties, personal cloud storage, code
repositories or unapproved AI tools. The full rules are the guide's section 4 and the
Digest's Part 3.

**Retention.** [CONFIRM: how long raw traces are kept on the device and in Hub; the NCAA
guide leaves the retention period pending General Counsel.]

## Teardown and storage

1. Stop recording and confirm the last save.
2. Confirm sync to VALD Hub if the device is online; if not, sync as soon as it is.
3. Power down the plates and the device.
4. Disconnect cables; coil, do not bend at the connector.
5. Wipe the plate surfaces.
6. Return everything to the case in its labeled spot and the case to its storage location
   [CONFIRM: location]. Put the device on charge.

## Who to contact

| Question | Contact |
|---|---|
| The protocol, cues, or whether to postpone a test | Director of Applied Performance |
| Running the test day to day, equipment location | [CONFIRM: Associate Director of Applied Performance or the daily user named above] |
| An athlete returning from injury | Athletic Medicine staff for that sport, then the Director |
| App, plates, Hub login | Vendor support through VALD Hub; then the Director |
| Data in the department database or the Wednesday read | [CONFIRM: owner of the force plate decision system] |

Phone numbers and emails live in the Digest appendix contact table, not here, so a staff
change does not orphan this chapter.

## Revision history

| Date | Author | Change | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-04 | Drafted for Eric Rash | First draft from the V3 protocol, the Operations Guide ForceDecks section, the SOP template, and the Iowa manual's format | 0.1 |

## Open questions for Eric

Answer these before the 10/23 ship date. Each one is also a [CONFIRM] tag above.

1. **Is V3 the live protocol?** Memory marks the Revised Force Plate Testing V3 protocol as
   "author uncertain." Is it what the staff run today, and is 3 reps still the count?
2. **Which ForceDecks app version is on the testing device?** The Operations Guide and V3
   use different button names. The chapter should match the screen.
3. **Soft landing or stiff landing?** V3 cues soft. Iowa cues stiff to read peak landing
   force. Soft is safer and matches practice, but it means landing-phase metrics are not
   comparable to published stiff-landing data. Keep soft and say so, or change?
4. **Who is the daily user and co-owner of this chapter?** The ship rule needs a named
   person who will run it, mark it up, and answer the 30-day check on 11/22.
5. **Which metrics are reported** for daily readiness and for coach reports, and is Jump
   Height (Imp-Mom) the variant in use?
6. **What is the live data path** from VALD Hub to Kitman Labs and to the department
   database? Which sports have the integration?
7. **Equipment facts:** plate model and serials, testing device name, storage location,
   vault name, sport code list, athlete ID source.
8. **Does this chapter replace the ForceDecks section of the Operations Guide** once it
